Correct
EXPLANATION

Recall that when a particle moves with constant acceleration, the velocity vector at time t can be found using

v=u+at,

where u is the initial velocity, and a is the acceleration of the particle.

Substituting

a=3i−2j,u=2i,v=14i−8j

into the equation above, we can solve for t, as follows:

v=u+at14i−8j=2i+(3i−2j)t12i−8j=(3i−2j)t12i−8j=3ti−2tj

Equating the i and j components in the last equation, we obtain {12=3t−8=−2t⟹t=4s.

h′(1)=
2

Correct
EXPLANATION

The quotient rule for derivatives gives h′(x)=f′(x)⋅g(x)−f(x)⋅g′(x)(g(x))2.

As a result, we have that h′(1)=f′(1)⋅g(1)−f(1)⋅g′(1)(g(1))2.

From the graphs above, we obtain that f(1)=2 and g(1)=1. Additionally:

  • The slope of f(x) on x∈(−1,3) equals 0. So, f′(1)=0.

  • The slope of g(x) on x∈(−1,3) equals −1. So, g′(1)=−1.

Finally, we have h′(1)=f′(1)⋅g(1)−f(1)⋅g′(1)(g(1))2=0⋅1−2⋅(−1)(1)2=21=2.
